payload.reason: The evidence discusses how embeddings are evaluated through their correlation with human similarity judgments and the performance of different models on datasets containing out-of-vocabulary items.

claims.text: Word-based embedding models correlate better with human judgments than character-based models, particularly for morphologically simple words.
Character-based models perform reasonably well on datasets with out-of-vocabulary words, indicating their competitive nature in similarity judgments.
The evaluation of embeddings includes comparing model word similarity scores with human similarity judgments, which is a standard measure of effectiveness.
